office_does: The sheriff is Klickitat County's elected chief law enforcement officer and runs the Sheriff's Office: patrol, investigations, search and rescue and marine patrol across the county.
race_blurb: Sheriff Bob Songer is retiring. Former deputy Dwayne Matulovich (Prefers Independent Party), who left the office in 2023, won 57% in the primary; Detective Sgt. Tony Warren (Prefers Republican Party), endorsed by Songer, had 27%. Warren says he might not enforce state laws he judges against residents' interest; Matulovich says that is for the courts. Neither would join the Constitutional Sheriffs and Peace Officers Association.

candidates.summary: Former Klickitat County deputy (2015-2023) and Goldendale and Bingen-White Salmon police officer, now a BNSF Railway welding foreman and volunteer firefighter, running to rebuild trust in the Sheriff's Office.
highlights: Wants more patrols and 'more thorough investigations' to 'start building that trust again' [S2]
Will improve deputies' training and morale and manage the budget responsibly [S1]
'My job is to enforce the laws. It's not to interpret them'; leaves constitutional questions to the courts [S3]
Will not join the Constitutional Sheriffs and Peace Officers Association [S3][S4]
Won 4,614 votes, about 57%, in the August primary [S5]

experience.basis: Left the Sheriff's Office in 2023 and runs against its current direction with no supervisory law-enforcement record, though with 19 years of police and deputy work.

safety.basis: Wants more patrols, more thorough investigations, more deputies and better training; no position on diversion or treatment found.

reform.basis: Says his experience shows 'what needs to be changed' and centres his campaign on rebuilding trust in the office after leaving it over its internal politics.

candidates.summary: Klickitat County Sheriff's Office detective sergeant (with the office since 2021) and former Bingen-White Salmon police officer and detective, endorsed by retiring Sheriff Bob Songer.
highlights: Wants three or four more deputies and faster, modernized records and reports [S4]
Lists drug enforcement, property crime and traffic safety, with community policing and regular deputy time in schools [S1][S3][S4]
Says he agrees with Songer 'on a lot of things' and may not enforce state laws he judges against residents' interest, 'within reason' [S5][S6]
Promises 'intentional, structural changes' (accountability standards, shift changes for deputy wellness) and to stay active on patrol rather than 'manage from behind the desk' [S3][S4]

City records show a 2014 suspension and a 2019 resignation during an internal investigation at the Bingen-White Salmon Police Department; his state separation notice listed no disqualifying misconduct, and he says the resignation followed allegations during his divorce [S4][S5]

experience.basis: Serving detective sergeant and the current sheriff's endorsed candidate, running as the only active officer in the race, but has not led the office.

safety.basis: Platform centres on more deputies and cracking down on drugs, property crime and abuse; his community policing and school presence are still policing, not services or diversion.

reform.basis: Campaign page promises 'comprehensive restructuring' and says endorsement 'does not mean duplication,' while he also says he agrees with the current sheriff on a lot.
